chunks: Then is the lowest class of the needy and the destitute

support of and help for whom is an obligation, and everyone of them has (a share in) livelihood in the name of Allāh. Everyone of them has a right on the ruler according to what is needed for his prosperity.

The ruler cannot acquit himself of the obligations laid on him by Allāh in this matter except by striving and seeking help from Allāh and by training himself to adhere to the right and by enduring on that account all that is light or hard.
ai.seo_question: What are the ruler's obligations towards the poor and destitute according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the support for the destitute as a mandatory right (haqq) upon the ruler, linking fiscal responsibility directly to spiritual discipline and steadfastness (sabr). This passage underscores the Shia political ideal that governance is not merely administrative but a divine trust requiring the ruler to internalize justice through self-purification and reliance on God, regardless of the burden's weight.
